speaker: Unknown
en: Asha, thank you so much for being here, and welcome to the podcast.
zh: Asha，非常感谢你来到这里，欢迎来到播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for having me.
zh: 谢谢你的邀请。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to start with something that we were chatting about before this that I've never heard about as a concept that I think is going to be really helpful for people to think about, which is this concept you have that we're moving from product as artifact to product as organism.
zh: 我想从我们之前聊过的一件事开始，我从未把它作为一个概念听说过，我认为这对人们思考非常有帮助，这就是你提出的概念，我们正从产品作为人工制品转向产品作为有机体。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk about what that means and what people need to understand here.
zh: 谈谈这意味着什么，以及人们需要理解什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's been a pretty interesting shift, especially over the last year or so because when I got to Microsoft, it was right after OpenAI and the large foundation models happened, and then immediately after there was this explosion of models, proprietary open frontier models that were pushing the frontier curve and so they were both more efficient and then we're starting to see domain level expertise in a bunch of them and then even more recently, models now can tool call and they can function call and they can take action, and I think that's just giving way to a new type of products that are starting to see some success.
zh: 这是一个相当有趣的转变，尤其是在过去一年左右，因为当我来到微软时，正好是在 OpenAI 和大型基础模型发生之后，紧接着就是模型的大爆发，专有的开放前沿模型推动着前沿曲线，所以它们更高效，然后我们开始看到其中许多模型的领域级专业知识，甚至在最近，模型现在可以进行工具调用，它们可以进行函数调用，它们可以采取行动，我认为这正在为一种新产品让路，这些产品开始看到一些成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so all of a sudden products aren't just like these static artifacts that we start to ship that's not just like, "Hey, come up with an idea or an insight.
zh: 突然间产品不再是我们开始发布的那种静态人工制品，不再只是，“嘿，想出一个主意或见解。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go solve a problem, ship it into the world, maybe make it a little bit better and then have a dashboard."
zh: 去解决问题，把它发布到世界上，也许让它变得好一点，然后有一个仪表板。”

speaker: Unknown
en: All of a sudden, the whole KPI is what is the metabolism of a product team to be able to ingest data and then digest the rewards model and then create some sort of outcome?
zh: 突然间，整个 KPI 就是产品团队的新陈代谢能力，能够摄取数据，然后消化奖励模型，然后创建某种结果？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because these models are so effective at this point, you want to start tune them to certain types of outcomes, whether it's price or performance or quality.
zh: 因为这些模型现在已经非常有效，你想要开始针对某些类型的结果来微调它们，无论是价格、性能还是质量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's pretty exciting because all of a sudden these are these living organisms that just get better with the more interactions that happen and in many ways I think this is the new IP of every single company and it's a completely different way to build product and to even think about products that think and live and learn, which is kind of exciting.
zh: 所以这非常令人兴奋，因为突然间这些是活的有机体，随着更多的交互发生而变得更好，在许多方面我认为这是每一家公司新的知识产权，这是一种完全不同的构建产品的方式，甚至思考那些会思考、会生活和会学习的产品的方式，这有点令人兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when I hear this, what I'm thinking about is when I had Michael Truell in the podcast, the Cursor CEO, he talked a lot about how their big moat is the data that they capture from people using Cursor, accepting certain suggestions, not accepting other suggestions.
zh: 所以当我听到这个时，我在想的是当 Michael Truell 来到播客时，那位 Cursor CEO，他谈了很多关于他们最大的护城河是他们从使用 Cursor 的人那里捕获的数据，接受某些建议，不接受其他建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that what you're talking about here?
zh: 这就是你在谈论的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Just the proprietary data that companies gather from people using their product or is there something beyond that even?
zh: 只是公司从使用其产品的人那里收集的专有数据，还是还有超越这一点的东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think why we're seeing the rise of post-training happen is just that the models themselves are so powerful.
zh: 我认为我们看到后训练兴起的原因只是模型本身是如此强大。

speaker: Unknown
en: As of this year, Nathan Lambert did this study that I thought was pretty interesting of all the top leader boards and it showed that once a model hits 30 billion parameters, the CapEx to actually train a model and put billions of tokens into a pre-run doesn't economically make sense and you can start to optimize on the loop.
zh: 到今年为止，Nathan Lambert 做了一项我认为很有趣的研究，针对所有顶级排行榜，结果显示一旦模型达到 300 亿参数，实际训练模型并投入数十亿 token 进行预运行所需的资本支出在经济上是不合理的，你可以开始在循环上进行优化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so yeah, in many ways, I think using your own data is the best way to do that, but you can synthetically generate data.
zh: 所以是的，在很多方面，我认为使用你自己的数据是最好的方法，但你也可以合成生成数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to come up with the rewards design, you have to actually roll it out, you have to A/B test it rigorously.
zh: 你必须想出奖励设计，你必须实际部署它，你必须严格地进行 A/B 测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to find the job to be done or the use case that it makes the most sense for.
zh: 你必须找到要完成的工作或它最有意义的用例。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then yes, that generates data that you can learn from.
zh: 然后是的，这会生成你可以从中学习的数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: I haven't ever seen it be one loop for any product.
zh: 对于任何产品，我从未见过它是单一循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's multiple tracks running in parallel that are like assembly lines, if you will, and producing that.
zh: 我认为这是多条并行运行的轨道，如果你愿意的话，就像流水线一样，并在生产那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so is this thesis that we're moving towards product as organism, is this basically for model companies or is this also true for, I don't know, SaaS businesses and tools and user tools?
zh: 那么这个我们正在迈向产品即有机体的论点，这基本上是针对模型公司的，还是这也适用于，我不知道，SaaS 业务、工具和用户工具？

speaker: Unknown
en: Look, I think that software as a primitive is changing and the artifact inside of it is a model alongside the software components itself.
zh: 听着，我认为软件作为一个原语正在改变，其中的产物是模型与软件组件本身并存。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so in many ways I think that software products will all be model forward products, if you will.
zh: 所以在很多方面，我认为软件产品都将是模型优先的产品，如果你愿意这么说的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: This reminds me what I just had Nick Turley on the podcast who we were talking about before we started recording head of ChatGPT and I was asking just like how much does ChatGPT change with GPT-5 coming out, and he's just like, "It's the same thing, they're the same product.
zh: 这让我想起我刚让 Nick Turley 上播客，我们在开始录音前谈论过他，他是 ChatGPT 的负责人，我就像问 ChatGPT 随 GPT-5 的推出会有多大变化，他就像说，“这是一回事，它们是同一个产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just the model tells us what to do in the product of ChatGPT."
zh: 只是模型告诉我们在 ChatGPT 这个产品中该做什么。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And it makes me think about something else of just you would think why can't just GPT-5 build its own user interface just like as you use it, it just evolve.
zh: 这让我想到另一件事，就是你会想为什么 GPT-5 不能建立自己的用户界面，就像当你使用它时，它只是进化。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's sort of what it's doing with Canvas and all these things, but that's another way I think about when you talk about this idea of product as organism is the product, the UX can shift based on how you're using it and evolve automatically without having product teams have to do anything.
zh: 这有点像它用 Canvas 和所有这些东西正在做的，但这是另一种我思考的方式，当你谈论产品即有机体这个概念时，产品，UX 可以根据你的使用方式转移，并自动进化，而不需要产品团队做任何事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I 100% believe that's where the world is going, and then my experience should look and feel different than yours.
zh: 我百分之百相信这就是世界发展的方向，然后我的体验看起来和感觉上应该与你的不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's been I've been in personalization, but now you can do it on the fly in the future.
zh: 我一直是在个性化领域，但现在你可以在未来即时地做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that'll be a pretty fun world.
zh: 所以我认为这将是一个相当有趣的世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: I also think it will look different for agents and it will look different for power users and new users and all of those things too.
zh: 我还认为它对于智能体来说看起来会有所不同，对于高级用户和新用户以及所有这些事情来说看起来也会有所不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me zoom out a little bit and ask you this question.
zh: 让我稍微zoom out一点并问你这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: You work with a bunch of companies that are building AI products on your platform, other platforms.
zh: 你与一群在你的平台、其他平台上构建 AI 产品的公司合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I imagine some just do an awesome job and are killing it, some are struggling.
zh: 我想有些做得非常好并且正在大杀四方，有些正在挣扎。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you find are common patterns across the companies that do really well and have a lot of success building really successful AI products and ones that don't?
zh: 你发现那些做得很好并在构建真正成功的 AI 产品方面取得很大成功的公司与那些没有的公司，有哪些共同模式？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so I think there's things that are more broadly applying to the organization themselves and then there's things that are applying to the people who are building the AI products too.
zh: 是的，所以我认为有更广泛适用于组织本身的事情，然后也有适用于构建 AI 产品的人员的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So more broadly, I think there's a pattern that's starting to emerge for successful companies.
zh: 所以更广泛地说，我认为有一种模式开始对成功的公司显现。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is they are embracing AI and everybody becomes AI fluent.
zh: 首先，他们正在拥抱 AI，每个人都变得 AI 流利。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think everybody is using some sort of co-pilot or sort of AI in their day-to-day workflows like job one, so everyone's not afraid of it, understands how we can raise the ceiling and lower the floor for all sorts of skills and tasks.
zh: 所以我认为每个人都在日常工作中使用某种副驾驶或某种 AI，作为工作第一要务，所以每个人都不害怕它，理解我们如何为各种技能和任务提升上限和降低下限。

speaker: Unknown
en: Number two, from there, they start to say, "Okay, how can I take a process that already exists and apply AI to making it better?"
zh: 第二，从那里开始，他们开始说，“好吧，我该如何采用一个已经存在的流程并应用 AI 使其变得更好？”

speaker: Unknown
en: That might be something like customer support or taking fraud down from 15 days to cure to 10 days.
zh: 这可能像客户支持，或者将欺诈解决时间从 15 天缩短到 10 天。

speaker: Unknown
en: In going through that entire loop of mapping out the process, applying AI to it, seeing some sort of impact, and then feeling the P&L or the intrinsic benefits that looks like.
zh: 在经历绘制流程图、应用 AI、看到某种影响，然后感受到损益或内在好处的整个循环中。

speaker: Unknown
en: The third thing then is like, "Okay, great.
zh: 第三件事就像，“好的，太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now that you've seen impact, everybody is using it, how do you actually use it to inflect growth?"
zh: 既然你已经看到了影响，每个人都在使用它，你实际上如何使用它来影响增长？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And that can be something like improving the customer experience, so your LTV or retention improves.
zh: 这可能是改善客户体验，所以你的 LTV 或留存率提高了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could be co-creating a new set of concepts or categories.
zh: 这可能是共同创造一套新的概念或类别。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could be going from agents that are embedded to agents that are embodied and then being able to take on exponential number of tasks.
zh: 这可能是从嵌入式智能体发展到具身智能体，然后能够承担指数数量的任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that where companies fail is that they're doing AI for AI's sake.
zh: 我认为公司失败的地方在于他们为了 AI 而 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have a ton of projects that they're kicking off at the same time without a blueprint to understand how it actually worked and what their Stack looks like and they aren't treating it like a real investment, and so they don't have the measurement and the observability and the evals all set up.
zh: 他们有大量的项目同时启动，没有蓝图去理解它是如何实际工作的以及他们的 Stack 是什么样的，而且他们没有把它像真正的投资一样对待，所以他们没有把测量、可观测性和 evals 都设置好。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going to do that end to end.
